name: The Chemistry
tagline: Foundational concepts and the beautiful complexity of chemical science.
seo_title: The Chemistry — foundations, news and innovations | Chemisters
seo_description: Follow Chemisters The Chemistry on LinkedIn and Facebook: the foundations of chemistry, field news and innovations.

definition.lead: Chemistry is the science of matter: what substances are made of, how their atoms are bonded, and how they change into other substances.
definition.body: Everything you can touch is chemistry, from the air you breathe to the screen you are reading. This page explores the foundations every chemist builds on: atoms, bonds, reactions, energy and the periodic table.

facts.label: elements, combining into more than 200 million registered substances
Avogadro's number: the number of particles in one mole
Lavoisier's 'Elementary Treatise of Chemistry', often seen as the start of modern chemistry

branches.name: Organic chemistry
branches.example: Medicines, plastics and the molecules of life.

branches.name: Inorganic chemistry
branches.summary: The chemistry of all the other elements, especially metals.

branches.name: Analytical chemistry
branches.summary: Finding out what is in a sample, and how much.

branches.name: Environmental chemistry
branches.summary: Chemicals in air, water and soil.

timeline.title: The Sceptical Chymist
timeline.text: Robert Boyle challenges ancient ideas about elements.

timeline.title: Modern chemistry
timeline.text: Antoine Lavoisier publishes his 'Elementary Treatise of Chemistry'.
timeline.why: Conservation of mass and a modern list of elements.

timeline.title: Atoms
timeline.text: John Dalton publishes his atomic theory.
timeline.why: Each element has its own kind of atom.

timeline.title: Molecules
timeline.text: Amedeo Avogadro proposes that equal gas volumes contain equal numbers of molecules.

timeline.title: The periodic table
timeline.text: Dmitri Mendeleev arranges the elements by their properties.

timeline.title: The electron
timeline.text: J. J. Thomson discovers the electron.

timeline.title: The nucleus
timeline.text: Ernest Rutherford shows that atoms have a tiny, dense nucleus.
timeline.why: The modern picture of the atom.

timeline.title: The chemical bond
timeline.text: Gilbert N. Lewis describes the covalent bond as a shared electron pair.

timeline.title: Quantum chemistry
timeline.text: Erwin Schrödinger publishes his wave equation.

timeline.title: The Nature of the Chemical Bond
timeline.text: Linus Pauling publishes his landmark book.
timeline.why: Brought quantum ideas to every chemist.

quiz.q: What does an atom's nucleus contain?
quiz.explain: Electrons occupy the space around the nucleus.

quiz.q: What defines which element an atom is?
How many particles are in one mole?

options: The attraction between positive and negative ions
A pair of electrons shared between two atoms
A hydrogen bond between two molecules
A nuclear force inside the atom

quiz.q: Who established the conservation of mass in chemical reactions?
quiz.explain: Matter is neither created nor destroyed in a reaction.

quiz.q: What did Rutherford's gold foil experiment reveal?
options: A tiny, dense, positively charged nucleus
quiz.explain: A few alpha particles bounced straight back.

quiz.q: Elements in the same group of the periodic table…
options: Have the same number of protons
quiz.explain: Because they have similar outer electron arrangements.

options: Speeds up a reaction without being used up

quiz.q: Which is the most abundant element in Earth's crust?
quiz.explain: Nearly half of the crust's mass, mostly in silicates.
